references.text: Parallel text that also commands all men to appear before the Lord three times a year at the three major festivals: the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles.
Repeats the command that all men must appear before the Lord, the God of Israel, three times a year.
Detailed description of the Lord's feasts, including Passover, the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks (Pentecost), and the Feast of Tabernacles.
The immediate context describing the details for each of the three festivals mentioned in verse 16.
Continuation explaining that every man must give according to his ability, as the Lord your God has blessed him.
Concerns the place where the Lord will choose to have His name dwell, where the Israelites shall bring their offerings.
Jesus goes up to Jerusalem for the Feast of Tabernacles, one of the three festivals mentioned in Deuteronomy.
Pentecost (the Feast of Weeks) when Jews from all nations were gathered in Jerusalem, in accordance with the command to appear before the Lord.
Paul wished to be in Jerusalem by Pentecost, showing the continued significance of the feasts.
